Thanks Michael — looked through the docs quickly. A few notes from procurement:

- Acme prefers a dedicated privateoffer SKU for trial entitlements to ensure entitlement tracking via our contract system.
- The pricing footnote is mostly fine but please avoid the phrasing "variable compute fees may apply"; our legal team wants a clearer table showing base price vs. optional burst pricing.
- Can you add a short snippet (1-2 lines) for our procurement playbook that explains how billing shows up on the Acme invoice when using a metered SKU vs privateoffer? That helps our SOW teams.

I’ll loop in the enablement contact at AWS if we need a seller-side SKU creation walkthrough.

Jordan — thanks for the clear guidance. Attaching the updated matrix and a short procurement snippet below. I also copied AWS seller enablement on this message in case we need direct SKU creation assistance.

Procurement snippet (paste-ready):
- Trial entitlement: Use the Acme privateoffer SKU (ID: to-be-created) for 14-day trials; billing shows as a privateoffer line item on Acme invoices and does not consume metered usage thresholds.
- Production/Pay-as-you-go: Use the metered SKU for on-demand consumption; invoice will show metered usage aggregated by month and include optional compute surcharges as separate line items if burst pricing is triggered.

Pricing footnote (summary):
- Base unit price: $0.15 per request (applies to standard inference profiles)
- Burst/Optional compute: billed per vGPU-hour when model execution exceeds baseline throughput; estimate shown for procurement transparency.
